title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Duty to Report vs. Confidentiality
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client privately reveals to their paralegal that their previous legal representative (a lawyer) embezzled $10,000 from their trust account. The client strictly forbids the paralegal from reporting this to the LSO because they fear retaliation. Does the paralegal have a mandatory duty to report the lawyer to the LSO?
options: Yes, the duty to report misappropriation of trust funds is absolute and overrides client confidentiality.
No, the duty to report misconduct to the LSO does not apply if the paralegal is reporting a lawyer, only another paralegal.
No, the duty to report is expressly subject to the duty of confidentiality and privilege owed to the client. If the client refuses consent, the paralegal cannot report it.
Yes, but the paralegal may submit an anonymous tip to satisfy both rules.
questions.explain: Rule 9.01 (Duty to Report) mandates reporting serious misconduct of other licensees. However, Rule 9.01(2) explicitly states that this rule does not override the duty of confidentiality owed to clients. If the client strictly forbids disclosure, the information is confidential/privileged, and the paralegal cannot report the former representative.
